1	# F4/G5 status-command failure safety — writer phase, 2026-11-01
2	
3	Writer phase only. Source written; **every test is UNRUN**. Nothing here claims runtime proof, goal or box acceptance,
4	a ledger entry or Done. Scope is the carried MB-1 F4/G5 shared-harness prerequisite, under the AUTH-01 S8/S2
5	shared-file ownership exception for exactly the seven paths below.
6	
7	## Why
8	
9	QA-9 phase 3N gap G5: the captured-output parse is guarded (`status-output.mjs`, accepted at 7/7 synthetic tests in
10	`harness-status-accepted-2026-11-01.md`). But `execFileSync` itself still throws when `pnpm exec supabase status -o json`
11	fails, and Node's `child_process` docs say that error carries the full `spawnSync` result: `stdout`, `stderr`,
12	`output`, `status`, `signal` and `pid`, with a message that names the command. In the three suites that error went
13	uncaught, so Node would print it with its fields. Captured stdout is status JSON, which holds the local keys. That breaks
14	PRD §22.1 (never log tokens).
15	
16	## Change
17	
18	- `scripts/backend/status-command.mjs` (new): `readLocalStatus(run = execFileSync)`. It runs the unchanged command
19	  `run('pnpm', ['exec', 'supabase', 'status', '-o', 'json'], { encoding: 'utf8', stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'] })`
20	  inside `try { … } catch { … }`. The catch has no binding, so the thrown value is never read. A failure throws
21	  `new Error(FAILED)`: one fixed message, no cause, no fields. Successful output goes to the existing
22	  `parseStatusOutput` outside the catch, so the parser's own fixed refusals are kept. Loading the module runs nothing:
23	  the real command is only the default of `run`. No change to environment, timeout, cwd or target.
24	- `scripts/backend/verify.mjs`, `verify-gym.mjs`, `verify-freezes.mjs`: the now-unused `node:child_process` and
25	  `status-output.mjs` imports become one `status-command.mjs` import. The status line becomes
26	  `const status|config = readLocalStatus();`. The exact-loopback assertion on the next line and every other byte
27	  (business assertions, cleanup) are unchanged.
28	- `scripts/backend/status-command.test.mjs` (new, written before the wrapper): 7 pure `node:test` tests, all with
29	  injected fakes:
30	  - Success as a string and as a Buffer: exactly one call, with the exact command, arguments and options.
31	  - Delegation to the parser: the same value, a near-miss target left unchanged, and the parser's own
32	    `NOT_JSON`/`NOT_OBJECT` refusals for malformed or non-object output.
33	  - Thrown error objects with a synthetic key and sentinel in message, stack, cause, stdout, stderr and output. Cases
34	    include timeout, failed start, AggregateError, a plain object and a Buffer.
35	  - Thrown primitives, including a string, BigInt and Symbol.
36	  - Getters on every field, and proxies that record every trap, proving the caught value is never touched.
37	  - A source gate checked before the dynamic import, so a regression cannot start the real command. It also checks
38	    that the catch has no binding and the parse sits after the catch.
39	  - Text-only checks of the three suites. They are never imported.
40	
41	  Every refusal is checked under message, `String`, stack, `inspect` (showHidden), JSON with and without hidden
42	  fields, and `structuredClone`.
43	- `scripts/backend/status-output.test.mjs`: only the wiring constants and the wiring test changed, to follow
44	  suite → wrapper → parser. It still requires: a single wrapper call in each suite; no child-process import or call and
45	  no parse in the suites; the unchanged command, run once in the wrapper, with the helper as its one parse; and the
46	  unchanged loopback assertion immediately after the call. The other six parser tests are byte-for-byte unchanged.
47	
48	Not touched: `status-output.mjs`, `local-stack.mjs`, `verify-identity.mjs`, replay files, package files, GOALS, the
49	ledger and main.
50	
51	## Verification still owed (UNRUN)
52	
53	The earlier 7/7 is historical, from before this change. Both pure files need a fresh, independent run by a separately
54	authorised verifier. The proposed exact pure commands (not run here) are:
55	
56	- `rtk proxy node --test scripts/backend/status-command.test.mjs`
57	- `rtk proxy node --test scripts/backend/status-output.test.mjs`
58	
59	RED was not observed: the test was written first against a missing module, but it was never executed. Mutation
60	checks, and suite syntax or execution, are also unproved. Do not run the three suites for this. They reach the
61	shared local stack.
62	
63	## Limits and residual owners
64	
65	- G1–G4, G6, G7 and the shared target binding stay open. Owner: MB-1 shared-harness prerequisites, verified under
66	  QA-9 phase 3N.
67	- By design, a failed status command now gives no exit code or stderr. To diagnose it, run the status command by hand
68	  in a trusted terminal.
69	- The hostile-value proof covers JavaScript-level reads only, not V8 or Node internals.
70	- Seen, not changed: `verify-freeze-projection.mjs` runs `JSON.parse(execFileSync('docker', … psql …))` with stderr
71	  piped. That is a different command, not status output. MB-1/QA-9 to triage whether it is in G5.
72	- QA-9 citation offsets remain QA-9-owned and non-blocking.

1	I've finished this writer phase. A failed `supabase status` command can no longer print its captured output, which holds the local keys. None of the tests have been run, so nothing here is proven at runtime yet.
2	
3	**What changed** (seven paths, Read/Grep/Edit/Write only, no denials):
4	1. `scripts/backend/status-command.mjs` (new): `readLocalStatus(run = execFileSync)`.
5	   - It runs the same `pnpm exec supabase status -o json` call with the same options.
6	   - If the command throws, the wrapper ignores the thrown value without reading it and throws a new error with one fixed message. That error has no cause and no other fields.
7	   - Successful output goes to the existing `parseStatusOutput`, outside that catch, so the parser's own refusals still come through.
8	   - Loading the file runs nothing. The real command is only the default for `run`.
9	2. `scripts/backend/status-command.test.mjs` (new, written before the wrapper): 7 tests, all with fake commands.
10	   - A check of the wrapper's source runs before the file is loaded. If someone later makes the wrapper run the command on load, the test fails instead of starting a real child process.
11	   - Success as a string and as a Buffer, with exactly one call and the exact command, arguments and options.
12	   - Output goes to the parser unchanged, and badly formed output still gets the parser's own refusal.
13	   - Thrown errors with a fake key in the message, stack, cause, stdout, stderr and output. Also thrown primitive values.
14	   - Hostile thrown values (getters and proxies) that record any access. They prove the wrapper never reads what was thrown.
15	   - Text-only checks of the three suites. They are never imported.
16	3. `verify.mjs`, `verify-gym.mjs`, `verify-freezes.mjs`: the two unused imports became one wrapper import, and the status line became `readLocalStatus()`. Every other byte is unchanged, including the loopback assertion on the next line.
17	4. `scripts/backend/status-output.test.mjs`: only the wiring constants and the wiring test changed, to follow suite → wrapper → parser. It checks everything it checked before. The other six tests are byte for byte unchanged.
18	5. `docs/evidence/MB-1/harness-command-failure-2026-11-01.md` (new): why, exact scope, the tests that still need running, limits and who owns what is left.
19	
20	**Self-review**
21	- **Critical / High:** none.
22	- **Medium 1:** RED, GREEN, the mutation checks and the suites' syntax are all unproven; I only traced the tests by hand. Both test files need a fresh run by a separate verifier, which the earlier 7/7 doesn't cover:
23	  - `rtk proxy node --test scripts/backend/status-command.test.mjs`
24	  - `rtk proxy node --test scripts/backend/status-output.test.mjs`
25	- **Medium 2 (not changed, out of scope):** `verify-freeze-projection.mjs` has a similar unguarded failure path: `JSON.parse(execFileSync('docker', … psql …))` with stderr piped. MB-1/QA-9 should decide whether it belongs to G5.
26	- **Low 1:** both test files check the three suites, so some checks overlap. The original brief and the scope correction each asked for them.
27	- **Low 2:** the load-time check is text matching. Contrived code could get past it, but ordinary edits make it fail.
28	- **Low 3:** this is by design. A failed status command now shows no exit code or stderr; to diagnose it, run the command by hand in a trusted terminal.
29	- **Low 4:** the hostile-value tests cover JavaScript-level reads only, not anything inside Node or V8.
30	- **Low 5:** I did not run the code-reviewer, security-reviewer or tdd-guide reviews (the brief bans sub-agents), and did not update `handoff.md` (it is outside the seven paths). Nothing is committed.
31	
32	G1–G4, G6, G7 and the shared target binding stay open with MB-1, verified under QA-9 phase 3N.
